statement: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is the distance all the way around it?

choices.misconception: I added one length and one width and stopped.
I added the two lengths and forgot both widths.
I multiplied the two measurements, which gives the space inside instead.
I counted four sides of 7 cm rather than two of each measurement.

hints: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths.
Walk round the shape and add a side at every corner. There are four sides, with the two lengths equal to each other and the two widths equal to each other.

solutions.reliable: The way round is 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 cm. The transferable idea: a rectangle has two of each measurement, so add all four sides, and multiplying the two numbers answers a different question entirely.

whyOnTest: Confusing the distance round with the space inside is the standard mix-up, and the multiplied answer is offered.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
